newsitem.title: UK: Wool production may fall 2.5 pct in 1996/7 - IWTO.
newsitem.headline: Wool production may fall 2.5 pct in 1996/7 - IWTO.

text.p: World wool production is seen contracting further during 1996/97 on the back of declining profitability, according to a report by the International Wool Textile Organisation.
Global wool production would fall by around 2.5 percent year-on-year during 1996/97 the IWTO said.
The fall would follow last season's five percent drop, the IWTO added, taking world wool production 27 percent below 1989/90 record levels.
The IWTO put global production prospects for 1996/97, based on official major producer clip estimates, at 2,456,000 tonnes greasy (1,422,000 clean), taking output to 1960s levels.
The former Soviet Union and Australia were expected to account for the entire reduction, the IWTO said, far outweighing the effect of continued expansion in China.
Smaller reductions were also anticipated for Argentina, the United States, the United Kingdom and Turkey, the report said.
New Zealand and South Africa would remain static, the IWTO said, while Uruguay's previous downtrend would reverse.

Australia's latest fall was due to a forecast 2.8 million drop in shearing numbers for sheep with lower than average fleece weights. Fleece weights are lower due to a higher proportion of lambs and ewes in the total of sheep shorn.
In South America, Argentinian output is expected to fall by around 4 percent to 78,000 tonnes greasy (41,000 clean) the IWTO said.
Production is down in most provinces, except Santa Cruz and Tierra del Fuego.
Sheep numbers have also dropped in the United Kingdom and in the United States to around 28 million each, the IWTO added. -Simon Gardner - London Newsroom + 44171 542 8057
